titleDv: ޤާނޫނު ނަންބަރު 9/2014 (ދިވެހިރާއްޖޭގެ ޤާނޫނުލްޢުޤޫބާތު) އަށް .. ވަނަ އިސްލާޙު ގެނައުމުގެ ބިލު
summary: This bill amends the Penal Code (Act No. 9/2014) to make dangerous driving of a land vehicle a separate criminal offence. It adds reckless driving to the list in Article 121(b), the situations presumed to be reckless conduct that could cause death or serious injury, alongside things like explosives, machinery and animals. It also adds a new Article 121-1 that defines the offence of dangerous driving: driving without regard for your own safety or the safety of other road users, in breach of the road traffic law and rules. Examples listed include speeding above the limit set under the Land Transport Act (Act No. 5/2009), dangerous overtaking and driving without a licence.
whyItMatters: Drivers who speed, overtake dangerously or drive without a licence could face criminal charges under the Penal Code, not only traffic fines, and people hurt in such accidents would have a criminal route to pursue the driver.
keyProvisions: Clause 1 adds item (7) to Article 121(b): driving a land vehicle in a way that causes fear or with disregard for the risk to someone's life is presumed to be a reckless act that could cause death or serious injury.

Clause 2 adds Article 121-1(a): driving a land vehicle dangerously, in breach of the standards in road traffic laws and rules and without regard for one's own safety or other road users' safety, is an offence.

Article 121-1(b) lists acts treated as dangerous driving: exceeding the top speed limit set under Act No. 5/2009 and its regulations, dangerous overtaking, driving without a driving licence, and other driving that disregards the danger to oneself or road users.
Article 121-1(c) grades the offence: it is a class 4 felony where the driving showed no regard at all for the driver's own or another person's life, and a class 1 misdemeanour in other cases.
Clause 3 says the amendment takes effect on the day it is ratified and published in the Government Gazette.
whoIsAffected: Drivers of cars, motorcycles and other land vehicles, people injured in road accidents, and police and prosecutors who handle traffic cases.
statedReasons: The note says Article 121 does not currently list reckless driving against road rules, so drivers in such accidents face no suitable action through the criminal justice system. The bill makes dangerous driving a separate offence so victims can get justice and drivers who break the Land Transport Act standards can be prosecuted.
